name: Purslane

facts.how: Raw for crunch, or cooked into eggs and stews (verdolagas)
facts.when: The hot months, June to September
facts.where: Sidewalk cracks, gardens, bare summer dirt
facts.value: Omega-3s, unusually rich for a green

caution: The look-alike is prostrate spurge: snap a stem, and milky white sap means spurge, drop it. Purslane bleeds clear.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: Fat, smooth, reddish stems hugging the ground with rubbery paddle leaves. It thrives in July heat that kills lettuce at forty paces.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Lemony crunch raw; silky when cooked. Across the border it is verdolagas, simmered with pork and tomatillo, which is the best argument for it.
